prompt: The point whose ordinate is 4 and which lies on the y-axis is:
markingScheme:
• Point lies on the y-axis ⇒ abscissa x = 0 [0.5 mark]
• Ordinate y = 4 ⇒ coordinates are (0, 4) [0.5 mark]
examinerTip: Common trap: Don't confuse (4, 0) which is on the x-axis with (0, 4) which is on the y-axis.

prompt: If the coordinates of two points are P(-2, 3) and Q(-3, 5), then (abscissa of P) - (abscissa of Q) is:
markingScheme:
• Abscissa of P = -2 [0.5 mark]
• Abscissa of Q = -3 ⇒ (-2) - (-3) = -2 + 3 = 1 [0.5 mark]
examinerTip: Be extremely vigilant with negative signs: (-2) - (-3) = +1.

prompt:
Assertion (A): The point (-a, 0) lies on the x-axis, and (0, b) lies on the y-axis.
Reason (R): Every point on the x-axis has a perpendicular distance of 0 from the x-axis, and every point on the y-axis has a perpendicular distance of 0 from the y-axis.
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
answer: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
markingScheme:
• Identifying that ordinate is 0 on x-axis and abscissa is 0 on y-axis [0.5 mark]
• Recognizing that distance from an axis equals the respective coordinate, so distance 0 implies lying on that axis [0.5 mark]
examinerTip: Direct question from PA-2 Class 9 CBSE examination paper.

prompt:
Write the quadrant or axis on which each of the following points lie:
(i) A(-3, 5)
(ii) B(4, -1)
(iii) C(0, -6)
(iv) D(-2, -7)
answer:
• A(-3, 5): Quadrant II (x < 0, y > 0)
• B(4, -1): Quadrant IV (x > 0, y < 0)
• C(0, -6): Negative y-axis (lies on axis, not in any quadrant)
• D(-2, -7): Quadrant III (x < 0, y < 0)
markingScheme:
• 0.5 mark for each correct identification.
• Specifying negative y-axis for C(0, -6): 0.5 mark.
examinerTip: Never write that (0, -6) lies in Quadrant III or IV. It lies strictly ON the y-axis.

prompt:
P(3, 2) and Q(7, 7) are two points in a Cartesian plane. Perpendiculars are drawn from P and Q to the x-axis meeting at L and M respectively.
(i) Find the coordinates of L and M.
(ii) Find the length of the segment LM.
(iii) What are the perpendicular distances of P and Q from the y-axis?
answer:
(i) Perpendicular from P(3, 2) to x-axis meets at L(3, 0). Perpendicular from Q(7, 7) to x-axis meets at M(7, 0).
(ii) Length of segment LM = |x_2 - x_1| = |7 - 3| = 4 units.
(iii) Perpendicular distance of P from y-axis = |3| = 3 units; for Q = |7| = 7 units.
markingScheme:
• Coordinates of L(3, 0) and M(7, 0): 1 mark (0.5 mark each)
• Calculation of length LM = 7 - 3 = 4 units: 1 mark
• Perpendicular distances from y-axis (3 and 7 units): 1 mark (0.5 mark each)
examinerTip: From school exam PA-2 Q29. Always state units for lengths and distances.

prompt:
A city planning department uses a Cartesian coordinate grid to map local public utilities, taking City Hall as the origin O(0, 0). 1 unit on the grid represents 500 meters.
• The Central Hospital is located at H(4, 3).
• The Fire Station is at F(-2, 3).
• The Police Station is at P(-2, -5).
• The Metro Hub is at M(4, -5).

Questions:
(i) In which quadrants do Central Hospital and Police Station lie? (1m)
(ii) What is the shape of quadrilateral HFPM formed by joining the four utilities in order? (1m)
(iii) Calculate the perimeter of quadrilateral HFPM on the grid and find the actual physical distance in kilometers. (2m)
answer:
(i) Central Hospital H(4, 3) lies in Quadrant I (+, +). Police Station P(-2, -5) lies in Quadrant III (-, -).

(ii) Line HF is horizontal: length = 4 - (-2) = 6 units.
Line FM is vertical: F(-2, 3) to P(-2, -5) has length = 3 - (-5) = 8 units.
Line PM is horizontal: length = 4 - (-2) = 6 units.
Line MH is vertical: length = 3 - (-5) = 8 units.
Opposite sides are equal and adjacent sides are perpendicular ⇒ HFPM is a Rectangle.

(iii) Perimeter on grid = 2 × (Length + Breadth) = 2 × (6 + 8) = 28 units.
Actual distance = 28 × 500 m = 14,000 m = 14 km.
markingScheme:
• (i) 0.5 mark for Quadrant I + 0.5 mark for Quadrant III = 1 mark
• (ii) Proving opposite sides equal and perpendicular angles ⇒ Rectangle: 1 mark
• (iii) Grid perimeter = 28 units: 1 mark; Conversion to km (14 km): 1 mark
examinerTip: In case-based coordinate geometry questions, always check if horizontal and vertical segments allow direct distance subtraction (|x_2 - x_1| or |y_2 - y_1|).
